paper.title: The Revised TESS Input Catalog and Candidate Target List

dataset.text: 修订后的 TESS Input Catalog (TIC) 可通过 Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (MAST) 服务器公开获取。
增强版的候选目标列表（CTL）可通过 Filtergraph 数据可视化门户系统在 http://filtergraph.vanderbilt.edu/tess_ctl 或 https://filtergraph.vanderbilt.edu/tess_ctl 获取。
TIC 和 CTL 附有官方发布说明，这些说明提供在 MAST 服务器上。
The base point source catalog consists of Gaia DR-2 and 2MASS point sources, totaling approximately 1.7 billion stars.
The base extended source catalog consists of 2MASS Extended, ALLWISE, and SDSS Extended sources, totaling approximately 1.6 million objects.

Spectroscopic parameters are sourced from multiple catalogs with defined priorities: SPOCS (1.6k stars, priority 1), PASTEL (93k stars, priority 2), Gaia-ESO DR-3 (29k stars, priority 3), TESS-HERMES DR-1 (25k stars, priority 4), GALAH DR-2 (340k stars, priority 5), and APOGEE-2 DR-14.

Specially curated lists including SuperBlink, Hot Subdwarf List, Guest Investigator Targets, and Hot Stuff for One Year (HSOY) are included in the TIC regardless of cross-match with the base catalogs.

Additional point source catalogs incorporated include Cool Dwarf List, UCAC 4 & 5, Tycho-2, APASS DR-9, ALLWISE point source, Gaia-TGAS, SDSS point source, Hipparcos, LAMOST DR-4, KIC + EPIC, RAVE DR-5, APOGEE, and SDSS DR-14.

Approximately 4 million stars were compared between the Pan-STARRS and Schlegel et al. (1998) dust maps.

The TIC uses provenance flags including Objtype, Typesrc, Posflag, and PMFlag to identify object types and data sources such as Gaia DR2, Hipparcos, 2MASS, cool dwarf lists, hot subdwarf lists, and GI programs.
TICv8 引入了新的来源标志（Provenance Flags），并在 Table 5 和 Table 6 中分别描述了早期版本和新版本的标志含义。

The catalog includes calculated TESS magnitudes.
Adopted effective temperatures (in K) are provided along with their sources and errors estimated via Monte Carlo methods.
Stellar radii and masses derived from photometry are included in solar units, with uncertainties and asymmetric Monte Carlo errors.
A contamination ratio representing the flux from neighboring stars relative to the target star is provided.
The catalog flags whether a star has been observed in 2-minute cadence and lists the sector or combination of sectors where it was observed.
Galactic and Ecliptic longitudes and latitudes in degrees are recorded for each star.
Parallaxes from TGAS/Gaia or Hipparcos, distances in parsecs, and total proper motions in mas/yr are provided with associated uncertainties including Monte Carlo estimates.
Photometric magnitudes from multiple surveys are included: V band, 2MASS JHKs, Gaia G/BP/RP, SDSS ugriz, and ALLWISE W1-W4.
Cross-identifiers include Hipparcos Number, Tycho-2 ID, 2MASS ID, and TICID from the TESS Input Catalog.
A flag identifies whether a star belongs to a special list.

Priority values are computed based on TIC-4, TIC-5, and TIC-6 schemas, as well as variants without neighbor contamination and without sector boosting, incorporating radius and flux contamination boosts and de-boosts.
Applied extinction E(B-V) values are provided with errors and source identification.
Additional stellar parameters include surface gravity (log g), density, luminosity, and metallicity, each with uncertainties and source identifiers.
Noise terms include uncertainties from star counts, sky counts, neighboring star counts, detector readout, and a systematics floor.

background.text: TESS Input Catalog (TIC) 是一个包含全天源的综合星表，用于 TESS 任务选择观测目标并提供评估凌星信号所需的恒星参数。
TIC 旨在为行星凌星搜索选择最优目标、计算每个目标在 TESS 孔径中的通量污染，并提供可靠的恒星半径以计算行星半径，从而决定哪些目标将获得任务支持的测光和光谱后续观测。
TIC 对于社区通过客座研究员（Guest Investigator）计划选择目标也是必不可少的。
TESS 每个像素投影的天空面积很大（21×21 角秒），点扩散函数半径通常为 1-2 个像素，因此给定 TESS 目标的测光孔径可能包含多个天体的通量。
因此，TIC 必须包含天空中每一个光学发光、持久且非移动的天体，直至现有宽视场测光点源星表的极限。
TESS 任务规划之初即预期 Gaia 任务提供的约 10 亿颗具有视差和自行的点源将成为 TIC 的理想基础星表。
由于 Gaia 数据发布进度原因，TESS 发射前仅有 Gaia DR1 可用，导致初始 TIC 仅包含 Tycho-Gaia Astrometric Solution (TGAS) 中约 200 万颗亮星的视差。
初始 TIC 中约 4.7 亿颗恒星的属性不得不基于宽带测光及复杂逻辑规则、算法和经验关系进行计算，其中部分需针对 TESS 波段定制。
由于具有测量视差的恒星数量很少，无法准确计算 TIC 中绝大多数恒星的半径，因此必须使用基于自行的标准来筛选候选目标列表（CTL）中的演化星。
根据 TESS 任务要求，从 CTL 中选择约 200,000 个目标进行 2 分钟步调的凌星搜索。
由于基于自行的方法无法区分亚巨星与矮星，旧版 CTL 不可避免地包含了大量亚巨星，估计多达约 50%。
为确保包含已知的高价值目标，TIC 和 CTL 曾由一系列特别策划的列表手动填充，包括亮星列表、冷矮星列表、已知行星宿主列表和热亚矮星列表。
TESS 发射后不久，Gaia 发布了第二次数据释放（DR2），包含 13 亿颗恒星的视差以及估计的恒星属性。
TICv7 was assembled for the first year of the TESS mission based on the 2MASS catalog, containing approximately 470 million point sources and 1.6 million extended objects.
TICv8 is an updated version of the TESS Input Catalog containing approximately 1.7 billion point sources and 1.6 million extended objects.
TESS Input Catalog (TIC) 中每个天体除位置外，最基本的需求量是其在 TESS 波段下的视星等。
TIC 中整合了多个光谱星表的数据，包括 LAMOST DR-4、RAVE DR-5、Geneva-Copenhagen DR-3 等。
TICv7 受限于当时的尘埃图，仅能估计沿银河系全视线方向的消光，且无法在银纬约 15 度以内估计红化。
由于恒星有效温度主要通过涉及 Gaia GBP-GRP 颜色的经验色指数关系估计，该颜色易受红化影响，因此需要先进行去红化改正。
Errors in dereddened effective temperature (Teff) can lead to inferring larger stellar radii and masses from empirical relations, making it important to assess the quality of dereddened Teff.
Both Gaia G and TESS T are broad photometric bands, which can complicate extinction corrections.
The ratio of total to selective extinction for the Gaia G band (RG ≡ AG/E(B-V)) is a function of Teff as well as the overall extinction AV.
Schlegel et al. (1998) dust maps have been shown to overestimate extinction for E(B-V) > 0.15 by a factor of about 1.4.
The Candidate Target List (CTL) provides a subset of TIC objects used to select target stars for TESS 2-minute cadence observations in service of the mission's primary science requirements.
TESS primary science requirement 1 is to search more than 200,000 stars for planets with orbital periods less than 10 days and radii smaller than 2.5 Earth radii.
TESS primary science requirement 2 is to search for transiting planets with radii smaller than 2.5 Earth radii and orbital periods up to 120 days among 10,000 stars in the ecliptic pole regions.
TESS primary science requirement 3 is to determine masses for at least 50 planets with radii smaller than 4 Earth radii.

Given the limited number of stars for which TESS can acquire 2-minute cadence light curves, the target set must be optimized for detection of small planets by compiling a catalog of bright dwarf stars across the sky.
The Candidate Target List (CTL) delivered to NASA is a list of candidate target stars with associated relative targeting priorities.
An enhanced version of the CTL is provided with all relevant observed and derived stellar quantities through the Filtergraph Portal system for community interaction.
TESS Input Catalog (TIC) 和 Candidate Target List (CTL) 中的目标优先级是选择适合2分钟采样观测的恒星候选体的基本特征之一。
TICv8 中 CTL 的目标优先级计算模式与 TICv7 完全相同，详细推导可参考 Stassun et al. (2018)。
TESS任务由NASA科学任务理事会提供资助。
本研究使用了欧洲空间局（ESA）Gaia任务的数据，该数据由Gaia数据处理与分析联盟（DPAC）处理。
There are approximately 3000 stars known to host exoplanets, of which about 2800 were discovered using radial velocity and transit methods.

TESS observations of known planet hosts are valuable for detecting stellar variability, refining transit ephemerides for follow-up, detecting transit timing variations to identify additional planets or companions, and discovering further transiting planets in those systems.
The paper describes the Revised TESS Input Catalog and Candidate Target List, which includes astrometric solutions for catalog objects.

discussion.text: 将估计的红化应用于通过测光颜色确定 Teff 的过程，通常会使得表观上较冷的恒星变得更热。
The variation of RG with AV is small (dRG/dAV ≈ -0.03) and can be ignored, but the variation with Teff is slightly larger and could be a reason for systematic trends seen in the Teff comparison.
A star that in reality has very low reddening could appear with E(B-V) > 2.5 if the dust map at that location is an extreme outlier, justifying the adoption of a 2.5 mag cap.

A discrepancy exists between the polynomial relation for the cooler BCG segment by Andrae et al. (2018) and their Figure 9, where BCG values extend more negative at the cool end in the figure than indicated by the polynomial; this was not reconciled but noted for completeness.

Simple summation in quadrature of underlying parameter errors overestimates the final uncertainty, which is particularly severe for the stellar radius because distance error enters four times, reddening map errors enter three times, Teff calibration error enters twice, and photometric errors in G_BP - G_RP enter twice.
Because CDC values are adopted as overrides, T magnitude offsets between CDC and nominal relations will only be noticeable when comparing similar stars where one is in the CDC and the other is not.
Stars with high Teff derived using photometric B magnitude should be checked independently before being used.

Not adopting curated parameters for known exoplanet hosts is not expected to have major effects on the TIC; all such stars remain listed with parameters no less reliable than similar TIC stars, though default pipeline transit properties may be less precise.
Individual investigators can recalculate transit properties themselves using published stellar information if needed.

experiments.text: Gaia 团队给出的 V 星等转换关系式的报道弥散约为 0.046 mag。
Pan-STARRS 与 Schlegel et al. (1998) 尘埃图给出的 E(B-V) 红化值对比显示总体一致性良好，在银纬 |b| > 15° 时差异在约 0.05 mag 以内。
The comparison of Teff obtained from dereddened colors versus spectroscopically measured Teff showed a mean difference of 20 K and a 95th percentile range of -410 K to +220 K.

There is a slight skew toward negative Teff differences (dereddened photometric Teff being slightly cooler than spectroscopic Teff), suggesting that in some cases the reddening is underestimated, though this is at the margins of the overall distribution.
Larger Teff errors are observed within approximately 10 degrees of the Galactic plane as a function of Galactic coordinates.
Only 1% of the approximately 4 million stars compared between Pan-STARRS and Schlegel et al. (1998) dust maps had applied E(B-V) values that disagree by more than 2.5 mag.
由于新的视差和MK标准，CDC2移除了CDC1中少量明亮且低温的条目。
例如，CDC1中最亮的天体半人马座α B（一颗K1矮星）因不满足新的MK标准而在CDC2中被移除。
CDC2相较于CDC1显著改善了南天（特别是南部连续观测区CVZ）的覆盖范围。
An offset of approximately 0.1 mag is observed between T magnitudes computed in the CDC versus nominal relations, reaching up to approximately 1 mag at the faintest end of the TIC (T ≳ 18).
Teff values computed in the CDC versus standard TIC relations are in good agreement, especially for Teff derived from Gaia colors, with scatter lower than the assumed 122 K for standard TIC Teff.
Stars with Teff inherited from TICv7 can differ more substantially, especially those with high Teff derived using photometric B magnitude (provenance flag 'bphotvk').
Comparison of identified cool dwarfs in TICv7 and TICv8 shows distribution changes in the top 400K targets.

limitations.text: Error propagation of TIC coordinates to epoch 2000 leads to much larger uncertainties than those native to nominal Gaia DR2 positions; users should use original Gaia DR2 positions, proper motions, and errors for forward propagation instead of TIC coordinates.

There were approximately 33 million cases of 2MASS sources with no Gaia counterpart, many expected to be 2MASS artifacts around bright stars, but they were left unaltered for TICv8 because no straightforward consistent identification method was found.

JHKs magnitudes are set to null for Gaia sources sharing a single 2MASS identifier to maintain catalog purity, although estimating them from Gaia fluxes using Evans et al. (2018) relations would be possible in principle.
将非对称误差平均化为对称误差时，某些情况下对称化后的误差可能大于物理量本身，这些情况需谨慎对待。
TESS 星等转换关系在应用于 M 矮星（GBP-GRP > 2）时性能显著下降。
使用恒星大气模型引入了系统误差，预测 T 星等的真实误差可能大于形式上的 0.006 mag。
作为非常保守的误差，指定了 0.6 mag，该误差对除最红 M 矮星以外的所有恒星应有效；最红的 M 矮星无论如何都通过专门策划的冷矮星列表处理。
The BC_G polynomial for the 8000–12000 K range must not be extrapolated beyond 12000 K, preventing computation of BC_G and parallax-based radii for stars with Teff > 12000 K.
Masses reported for subgiant stars should be regarded with caution because the Teff-mass relation implicitly applies to them despite being calibrated for main-sequence stars.
The PSF model used for calculating flux contamination does not attempt to account for bleed trails from very bright stars.
用于估计 T_eff 的关系式在 15000 K 处截止，分布中更热的恒星来源于专门策划的热亚矮星列表。
半径 R ≥ 5 R⊙ 的恒星被视为巨星，不为其报告质量或其他衍生属性。
质量关系式主要针对矮星设计，对亚巨星也能可靠工作，但对巨星不可靠。
Catalogs of exoplanet host parameters, including the NASA Exoplanet Archive, are inherently incomplete and heterogeneous, preventing their adoption without compromising TIC internal consistency.
The absence of highly curated stellar parameters for known planet hosts results in less precise determination of transit properties from the default TESS transit search pipeline.

methodology.text: 本文描述了基于整合 Gaia 第二次数据释放（DR2）所组装的星表以及用于填充修订版 TESS Input Catalog (TIC) 的算法。
研究描述了一种修订后的排序系统，用于对 2 分钟步调观测的恒星进行优先级排序，并使用该排序组装了修订后的候选目标列表（CTL）。
Gaia DR2 提供的三个波段（G、GBP、GRP）的均匀测光极大地简化了通过一组更小、更统一的算法和经验关系来计算各种恒星属性的过程。
论文第 2 节详细描述了 TIC 的构建以及用于计算各种恒星量的算法；第 3 节描述了 CTL 的构建、CTL 特有参数的附加算法以及 2 分钟步调观测目标选择的优先级方案。
TIC 故意同时包含点源（恒星）和延展源（如星系），可以通过 objtype_flag 标志将它们分开。
第一年版 TIC 采用 2MASS 星表作为基础点源星表，并将所有其他数据交叉参考到 2MASS 点源，当时因 Gaia DR2 尚未发布而仅使用了 Gaia DR1 视差。
当前版本的 TIC 已使用 Gaia DR2 作为基础进行了重建。

The base point-source catalog for the TIC is Gaia DR2, replacing the previous 2MASS-based approach to preserve continuity and provenance by translating previous TIC sources using the Gaia-2MASS association provided within Gaia DR2.
TIC coordinates and their uncertainties were propagated to epoch 2000 due to mission requirements.

Due to improved angular resolution and depth of Gaia DR2 relative to 2MASS, cases where a single 2MASS source associated with two Gaia sources retained the 2MASS identifier for both but set JHKs magnitudes to null because there was no definitive means for splitting the reported 2MASS flux.
For the purposes of the TIC, only the Gaia reported G, GBP, and GRP magnitudes are required, with corrections applied for bright stars (G < 6) as reported by Evans et al. (2018).

While stellar properties for most TIC stars are calculated from Gaia magnitudes via relations, measured spectroscopic parameters are adopted where possible, selecting effective temperatures and metallicities from catalogs in a defined order of preference.

Surface gravities (log g) in TICv8 are always calculated using the TICv8 reported mass and radius rather than adopted from spectroscopic catalogs, ensuring internal consistency of log g with mass and radius.
Metallicities are reported when available from spectroscopic catalogs for convenience only and are not used in any relations or derived quantities in the TIC.
Quantities from large catalogs such as ALLWISE and SDSS are incorporated for objects that cross-match with the Base Extended Source Catalog or base catalogs.
论文描述了用于计算各种恒星参数的算法流程，首先从计算 TESS 波段视星等开始。
有效温度（Teff）优先采用光谱测量值（若报告误差小于 300 K），否则通过经验关系由测光颜色计算得出。
在使用测光颜色之前，必须先对其进行消红化修正。
基于 Gaia DR2 的天体测量和测光质量标志进行筛选，未通过质量标准的天体不计算其他恒星参数；若 TICv7 中已计算过则沿用旧参数。
涉及 Gaia DR2 视差时，采用 Bailer-Jones 等人 (2018) 的贝叶斯距离估计，以提供适当的后验误差估计并确保距离非负。
由于 TIC 要求报告对称误差条，因此对 CTL 天体确定的非对称误差取算术平均值作为对称误差。
TESS 星等关系基于 PHOENIX 模型大气以及最新的 TESS 通带和 Gaia G、GBP、GRP 通带推导得出。
在构建基础 TIC 时未应用 Maíz Apellániz 等人 (2018) 对 Gaia 通带的微小修正。
TESS 星等与 Gaia 颜色的关系被拟合为一个三次多项式，适用于任何金属丰度的矮星、亚巨星和巨星，形式散射为 0.006 mag。
该 TESS 星等关系严格适用于 -0.2 < GBP-GRP < 3.5，但为满足 NASA 要求每颗恒星都有 T 星等的规定，外推至 -1.0 < GBP-GRP < 6.0。
尽管该关系对 M 矮星退化明显，但仍被认为是从 G 星等出发的最佳可用估计；特别策划的冷矮星列表中提供的精细 T 星等会覆盖上述计算结果。
通过将相同大气模型导出的 V 星等与 Gaia 星等关系同 Evans 等人 (2018) 的经验关系进行比较来估计系统误差，两者最大差异仅约 0.1 mag，表明真实不确定度最多约为 0.1 mag。
TESS 星等关系严格适用于未红化恒星；实际操作中先对颜色和 G 星等进行消红化和消光修正，计算去红化 T 星等后再加回消光以获得视星等。
对于颜色超出关系正式有效范围的恒星，外推同一多项式，但保守地将形式误差增加 0.1 mag（正交相加）。
对于没有有效 GBP-GRP 颜色但有有效 G 星等的恒星，使用简单的偏移量 T = G - 0.430，该值对应类似太阳的恒星。
对于 TICv7 中没有测量 V 星等但具有 Gaia 测光的 TIC 恒星，使用 Gaia 团队（Evans et al. 2018）提供的关系式计算视 V 星等：V = G + 0.01760 + 0.006860(GBP-GRP) + 0.1732(GBP-GRP)^2。
本研究采用 Pan-STARRS 新发布的三维、经验性、近全天尘埃图（Green et al. 2018），以根据恒星在三维空间中的位置逐星估计红化。
对于 Pan-STARRS 未覆盖的天区（赤纬低于 -30°），继续使用 Schlegel et al. (1998) 尘埃图，并结合 Gaia 距离对总视线方向消光进行调整，假设盘面为标高高 125 pc 的标准指数模型。
在上述两种情况下，均按 Schlafly & Finkbeiner (2011) 的规定对 E(B-V) 值应用 0.884 的重新标定系数。
为将尘埃图提供的 E(B-V) 转换为 E(GBP-GRP) 和 AG 以去红化 Gaia 颜色，使用类太阳合成光谱（PHOENIX 模型，Teff=5800 K, log g=4.5, [Fe/H]=0.0）按 Casagrande & VandenBerg (2014) 公式计算各通带有效波长。
利用上述平均波长结合 Cardelli et al. (1989) 消光律，得到 E(GBP-GRP) = 1.31 E(B-V) 以及 AG = 2.72 E(B-V)。
通过相同程序确定 E(B-V) 与 TESS 波段消光 A(T) 的关系，用于计算 T 星等，结果为 A(T) = 2.06 E(B-V)。

The sample used to compare spectroscopic and photometric Teff was limited to stars whose spectroscopic Teff have reported uncertainties less than 300 K to ensure that spectroscopic errors do not dominate the comparison.
A new empirical relation between Teff and Gaia GBP-GRP colors was derived based on a set of 19,962 stars having spectroscopically determined Teff and being within 100 pc to avoid reddening.
After removing obvious outliers from the calibration sample, a spline function was fit by eye to relate GBP-GRP colors to Teff.

Based on comparisons between Pan-STARRS and Schlegel et al. (1998) dust maps, 2.5 mag is adopted as the maximum permissible E(B-V) from the Schlegel et al. (1998) dust map (effectively capping AV at ≈ 7.8) when a reliable Pan-STARRS value is not available.

In cases where there is no reliable Pan-STARRS value and the adopted Schlegel et al. (1998) value has been capped, the values are reported but no reddening is applied in calculating the T magnitude, and no derived stellar parameters are provided.
The CTL priority is reduced by a factor of 0.1 for stars within 10 degrees of the Galactic plane due to larger errors.
The fit residuals of the photometric color–Teff relation show a near-zero mean offset with an r.m.s. scatter of 122 K.
Given typical spectroscopic Teff uncertainties of ~100 K, the true scatter in the photometric relation is implied to be ~70 K.
The validity range of the color–Teff relation is GBP-GRP = [-0.2, +3.5].
Predictions from the color–Teff relation are likely less reliable for hot stars with GBP-GRP < 0 due to the steep slope, and for M stars with GBP-GRP > 2.
The CTL relies mainly on a specially curated Cool Dwarf list for cool dwarf stars and draws Teff estimates for those stars from that list.
The color–Teff relation provides a continuous relation from 3000 K to 15000 K; outside this range the TIC reports Teff = Null unless a spectroscopic Teff or a CTL-associated Teff is available.
Final Teff errors reported in the TIC include the 122 K scatter added in quadrature to uncertainties from photometric errors.
Stellar radii are computed using Gaia parallaxes via the standard Stefan-Boltzmann relation involving distance, extinction-corrected G magnitude, Teff, and bolometric correction in the Gaia passband.

Distance D is based on Gaia parallax from Bailer-Jones et al. (2018), G is extinction-corrected observed Gaia magnitude, Teff is from spectroscopy or dereddened colors, and BCG is the bolometric correction as a function of Teff.
For Teff from spectroscopy, 100 K is added in quadrature to the Teff uncertainty if the catalog-reported uncertainty is less than 100 K when computing mass and radius uncertainties.

For the 3300–8000 K range, polynomial formulae for BCG reported by the Gaia team (Andrae et al. 2018) based on MARCS models within 0.5 dex of solar metallicity are adopted, split into 3300–4000 K and 4000–8000 K segments with a +0.0036 mag shift applied to the cooler segment for continuity.

Above 8000 K up to 12000 K, a cubic polynomial is fit to bolometric corrections from PHOENIX stellar atmosphere models restricted to metallicities within 0.5 dex of solar and log g above 3.0, shifted by +0.01036 mag to match the Gaia polynomial at 8000 K, with a constant BCG error of 0.04 mag adopted.

The study provides polynomial relations to compute the Gaia G-band bolometric correction (BC_G) as a function of effective temperature for three ranges: below 4000 K, 4000–8000 K, and 8000–12000 K, along with corresponding uncertainty polynomials.

Stellar mass is inferred from effective temperature using revised spline relations for stars on or near the main sequence, applied only when the stellar radius places the star below the red giant branch and above the white dwarf sequence.
For stars cooler than 3300 K, stellar parameters are adopted from a specially curated Cool Dwarf list rather than extrapolating the Gaia polynomial relation.

To ensure internal consistency, dependent stellar properties such as log g, mean density, and bolometric luminosity are always calculated from the determined effective temperature, radius, and mass rather than using empirical measures from other catalogs.

The CTL assembly approach starts with approximately 1.7 billion stars in the TIC and applies cuts to select stars within desired apparent magnitude and spectral type ranges while eliminating evolved stars.

Stars are initially selected for the CTL if they have parallaxes and Gaia DR2 G, G_BP, and G_RP photometry satisfying quality criteria on reduced chi-squared, degrees of freedom, photometric excess factor, and color indices.
A TESS magnitude cut of T < 13 is applied to reduce the CTL to a manageable size, emphasizing bright dwarfs likely to be highest priority targets.
A specially curated Cool Dwarf List is used to ensure inclusion of high-priority M-dwarfs that would otherwise be eliminated by the T < 13 magnitude cut.

Stellar radius cuts are applied to eliminate red giants, explicitly including subgiants with 3.5 < log g < 4.1 but relying on prioritization metrics to prevent them from overwhelming final target selection.
For Teff >= 6000 K, the dividing line for radius cuts is log(R/R_sun) = 0.7, with subsequent piecewise linear nodes at (5000 K, 0.2) and (2000 K, 0.0).
Stars likely to be white dwarfs are excluded using a diagram of absolute G magnitude versus G_BP - G_RP color.
A color-magnitude boundary was defined by eye in the M_G vs G_BP - G_RP diagram to separate main sequence and white dwarf sequences, represented by the equation M_G = 5.15(G_BP - G_RP) + 4.12.
Stars falling below the defined color-magnitude boundary after proper reddening corrections are eliminated as probable white dwarfs.

Stars are excluded from the CTL if their effective temperature cannot be determined spectroscopically or from dereddened colors, or if their radius or flux contamination from nearby stars cannot be estimated, as these are essential for setting target priorities.
All stars in the specially curated Cool Dwarf and Hot Subdwarf target lists are included in the CTL.

Stars previously included in the TICv7 CTL based on reduced proper-motion cuts suggesting they are dwarfs are retained in the new CTL if Gaia DR2 does not provide sufficiently reliable information to warrant their exclusion.

Flux contamination is calculated by searching for contaminants within 10 TESS pixels of the target and computing contaminating flux within a magnitude-dependent radius using a pre-launch PSF model from SPOC; the reported value is the ratio of total contaminant flux to target star flux.

A Monte Carlo approach is implemented to improve final uncertainty estimates for stellar parameters by perturbing each observed quantity 1000 times and carrying perturbed values through calculations to obtain distributions for each derived quantity.
The 16th and 84th percentiles of the Monte Carlo derived distributions are reported as the corresponding lower and upper error bars to reflect asymmetric parameter posteriors.

Once a quantity is perturbed in the Monte Carlo procedure, the same perturbed value is used throughout to preserve parameter correlations; asymmetric errors are handled by assuming Gaussian distributions on each side.

The Monte Carlo procedure sequentially perturbs the stellar distance using normal Gaussian deviates and then perturbs the reddening based on contributions from both distance and intrinsic dust map errors.

The method perturbs the (B-V) color by adding Gaussian noise scaled by the low and high reddening uncertainties, then calculates reddening and extinction in Gaia passbands using E(G_BP-G_RP)' = 1.31 E(B-V)' and A(G)' = 2.72 E(B-V)'.
Gaia color and magnitude are perturbed using photometric errors: (G_BP-G_RP)' = (G_BP-G_RP) + N×σ_G_BP + N×σ_G_RP, and G' = G + N×σ_G.
The perturbed Gaia color and magnitude are dereddened by subtracting the calculated reddening and extinction values.

The perturbed and dereddened TESS magnitude is computed using dereddened Gaia magnitude and color, with perturbed T-band extinction applied as A(T)' = 2.06 E(B-V)'. The final apparent TESS magnitude includes this extinction plus scatter from the T calibration.
The perturbed effective temperature is computed by adding Gaussian noise to the perturbed dereddened temperature, where σ_Teff = 122 K.
The perturbed stellar radius is computed from the perturbed bolometric correction, effective temperature, distance, and dereddened Gaia magnitude.
扰动质量 M' 的计算公式为 M(T'_eff) + N × {σ_M,low, σ_M,high}，其中 σ_M 是 T'_eff 的函数。
基于扰动质量和半径，进一步计算扰动的 log g、光度和平均密度，公式分别为 log g' = 4.4383 + log M' - 2 log R'，L' = (R')^2 (T'_eff/5772)^4，以及 ρ' = M'/(R')^3。
TICv8 中的优先级决定了 TESS 探测小行星凌星的相对能力，其计算使用恒星半径 (R)、总预期测光精度 (σ) 以及与预期扇区数 (N_S) 概率模型成比例的优先级提升因子。
越靠近黄道北极或南极的恒星，其优先级提升因子越大。
恒星优先级的计算公式包含 √N_S / (R^1.5 × σ)，并通过 R=0.1 R⊙、N_S=12.654 扇区和 σ=61.75 ppm 的参考星进行归一化，使优先级处于 0 到 1 之间。
对于银纬 |b| < 10° 的恒星，由于对其真实红化的理解较差，其优先级乘以 0.1 的系数以降低优先级，但特别策划列表中的恒星除外。
log g 大于 5 的恒星的优先级被设为 0，属性被设为 Null，以避免有效温度、消光或视差测量质量差带来的偏差；特别策划列表中的恒星不受此条件限制。
黄纬 |β| ≲ 6° 的恒星由于南北观测之间的相机覆盖间隙，预计不会在主任务中被观测到，因此其 N_S 值为 0，优先级也为 0。
TICv7中关于冷有效温度、小半径和低质量的子群体数量反映的是CTLv7的数值，因为在TICv7中这些量仅对CTL中的恒星进行了计算。
TICv7的特选列表在TICv8中得到了更新。
冷矮星列表已更新并作为总覆盖项并入TIC和CTL，即该列表中的值取代并替换通常TIC/CTL程序计算的默认值。
对于TICv8，冷矮星特选列表被修订并大幅扩充，纳入了Gaia任务新提供的天体测量视差和测光数据。
第二版冷矮星目录（CDC2）是通过Gaia DR2源与2MASS点源目录（2MASS PSC）之间的最近邻交叉匹配构建的。
交叉匹配目录的查询标准要求具有非零天体测量视差且信噪比至少为5。
查询标准要求目标在2MASS PSC中具有唯一条目，且所有2MASS星等的测光质量标志为C或更好。
查询标准包括绝对Ks波段星等（MKs）介于4.5和10.0之间。
为识别冷星并与CDC1保持一致，要求V-J颜色大于2.7。
绝对V波段星等（MV）需满足 MV > 2.2(V-J) - 2 的标准。
查询标准要求Gaia GRP波段星等小于18。
绝对星等计算中使用的距离取自Bailer-Jones等人（2018）。
V波段星等是利用GBP和GRP星等以及Jao等人（2018）发表的转换关系计算得出的。
查询过程中未应用任何消光或红化校正。
查询结果与原始冷矮星目录（CDC1）进行了交叉匹配，包含了两个目录中的所有条目。
假设每个条目为单星并忽略红化和消光影响，计算了每个条目的恒星质量、半径、有效温度和TESS星等。
恒星质量和半径分别使用Mann等人（2019）的质量-MK关系和Mann等人（2015）的半径-MK关系计算，两者均适用于4.5 < MK < 10.0的范围。
超出上述MK范围或缺乏天体测量视差的物体被标记为移除。
有效温度和TESS星等是使用基于Mann等人（2013）测光校准光谱开发的自定义关系，从GBP和GRP星等计算得出的。
CDC1中没有唯一2MASS标识符的天体被标记为移除。
本研究广泛使用了Filtergraph数据可视化服务。
本研究使用了位于法国斯特拉斯堡CDS运行的SIMBAD数据库和VizieR星表访问工具，以及NASA的天体物理数据系统（ADS）。
The CDC values are adopted as an override for T magnitudes when available.
All known planet hosts are included in the updated TIC, with stellar parameters determined according to standard procedures rather than curated individual measurements.

The authors decided not to adopt curated exoplanet host star parameters from external catalogs because such catalogs are incomplete and heterogeneous, requiring star-by-star customization that would compromise internal consistency.
The bright stars list no longer exists as a specially curated list; bright stars are included in the TIC without separate procedures or special priorities.
Hot subdwarfs have been updated and are incorporated into the TIC and CTL as a total override.
Proposed Guest Investigator Cycle 2 targets without pre-existing TIC-IDs are imported as new objects.
Proper motions in the catalog are sourced from multiple databases including SuperBlink, Tycho2, Hipparcos, UCAC5, and Hot Stuff for One Year (HSOY).
Parallaxes are derived from Gaia DR-2, Tycho2-Gaia Astrometric Solution (TGAS), or Hipparcos, with a PARFlag used to identify the source of the object's parallax.
A TESSFlag is used to identify the source of the object's T magnitude.
TESS magnitudes are calculated using various methods including offsets with Gaia magnitudes, Gaia BP-RP colors, 2MASS photometry, Hipparcos V magnitudes, and combinations thereof.
Magnitudes are also adopted directly from external lists such as the hot subdwarf list, the cool dwarf list (Muirhead et al. 2018), the Lepine catalog, and GI Cycle 1 proposals.
TICv8 使用 SPFlag 字段标识天体恒星参数的来源，包括来自冷矮星列表（cdwrf）、热亚矮星列表（hotsd）、基于 TGAS 视差计算（gaia2）、光谱 Torres 关系计算（spec7）以及从 TICv7 导入（tic7）。
TICv8 引入 EBVFlag 标识红化来源：距离小于 100 pc 时不应用消光（0），或分别采用 Schlegel 等（1998）（1）和 Green 等（2018）（2）的红化值。
TeffFlag 用于标识有效温度来源，包括冷矮星列表（cdwrf）、热亚矮星列表（hotsd）、光谱星表（spect）、Gaia G_BP-G_RP 颜色（gaia2）以及从 TICv7 导入（spec）。
gaiaqflag 用于标识 Gaia 天体测量与测光信息的质量，分为信息不足（-1）、质量差（0）和质量好（1）。
Vmagflag 标识 V 星等来源，包括由 Gaia G_BP-G_RP 颜色计算、UCAC4、Tycho-V_T、APASS DR-9/DR-7、SuperBlink、Mermilloid、冷矮星列表、Sirful、Hipparcos V 以及 Gaia DR-1 G 与 2MASS K_S 计算等多种途径。
Bmagflag 标识 B 星等来源，包括由 Tycho-B_T 计算、APASS DR-9 导入、2MASS 测光 B 计算以及 Mermilloid 星表导入等。
splists 字段标识天体是否属于特别策划的列表，如冷矮星列表（cooldwarfs v8）或热亚矮星列表（hotsubdwarfs v8）。
增强的 CTL 内容通过 Filtergraph 数据可视化门户服务（filtergraph.vanderbilt.edu/tess_ctl）提供，包含赤经（J2000.0, epoch 2000.0）和赤纬等列。
The paper provides a basic description of all quantities available on the Filtergraph portal for the TESS Input Catalog.

paragraphs.text: TESS Input Catalog (TIC) 是一个包含全天源的综合星表，用于 TESS 任务选择观测目标并提供评估凌星信号所需的恒星参数。
TIC 旨在为行星凌星搜索选择最优目标、计算每个目标在 TESS 孔径中的通量污染，并提供可靠的恒星半径以计算行星半径，从而决定哪些目标将获得任务支持的测光和光谱后续观测。
TIC 对于社区通过客座研究员（Guest Investigator）计划选择目标也是必不可少的。
TESS 每个像素投影的天空面积很大（21×21 角秒），点扩散函数半径通常为 1-2 个像素，因此给定 TESS 目标的测光孔径可能包含多个天体的通量。
因此，TIC 必须包含天空中每一个光学发光、持久且非移动的天体，直至现有宽视场测光点源星表的极限。
TESS 任务规划之初即预期 Gaia 任务提供的约 10 亿颗具有视差和自行的点源将成为 TIC 的理想基础星表。
由于 Gaia 数据发布进度原因，TESS 发射前仅有 Gaia DR1 可用，导致初始 TIC 仅包含 Tycho-Gaia Astrometric Solution (TGAS) 中约 200 万颗亮星的视差。
初始 TIC 中约 4.7 亿颗恒星的属性不得不基于宽带测光及复杂逻辑规则、算法和经验关系进行计算，其中部分需针对 TESS 波段定制。
由于具有测量视差的恒星数量很少，无法准确计算 TIC 中绝大多数恒星的半径，因此必须使用基于自行的标准来筛选候选目标列表（CTL）中的演化星。
根据 TESS 任务要求，从 CTL 中选择约 200,000 个目标进行 2 分钟步调的凌星搜索。
由于基于自行的方法无法区分亚巨星与矮星，旧版 CTL 不可避免地包含了大量亚巨星，估计多达约 50%。
为确保包含已知的高价值目标，TIC 和 CTL 曾由一系列特别策划的列表手动填充，包括亮星列表、冷矮星列表、已知行星宿主列表和热亚矮星列表。
TESS 发射后不久，Gaia 发布了第二次数据释放（DR2），包含 13 亿颗恒星的视差以及估计的恒星属性。
TICv7 was assembled for the first year of the TESS mission based on the 2MASS catalog, containing approximately 470 million point sources and 1.6 million extended objects.
TICv8 is an updated version of the TESS Input Catalog containing approximately 1.7 billion point sources and 1.6 million extended objects.
TESS Input Catalog (TIC) 中每个天体除位置外，最基本的需求量是其在 TESS 波段下的视星等。
TIC 中整合了多个光谱星表的数据，包括 LAMOST DR-4、RAVE DR-5、Geneva-Copenhagen DR-3 等。
TICv7 受限于当时的尘埃图，仅能估计沿银河系全视线方向的消光，且无法在银纬约 15 度以内估计红化。
由于恒星有效温度主要通过涉及 Gaia GBP-GRP 颜色的经验色指数关系估计，该颜色易受红化影响，因此需要先进行去红化改正。

The sample used to compare spectroscopic and photometric Teff was limited to stars whose spectroscopic Teff have reported uncertainties less than 300 K to ensure that spectroscopic errors do not dominate the comparison.
A new empirical relation between Teff and Gaia GBP-GRP colors was derived based on a set of 19,962 stars having spectroscopically determined Teff and being within 100 pc to avoid reddening.
After removing obvious outliers from the calibration sample, a spline function was fit by eye to relate GBP-GRP colors to Teff.

Based on comparisons between Pan-STARRS and Schlegel et al. (1998) dust maps, 2.5 mag is adopted as the maximum permissible E(B-V) from the Schlegel et al. (1998) dust map (effectively capping AV at ≈ 7.8) when a reliable Pan-STARRS value is not available.

In cases where there is no reliable Pan-STARRS value and the adopted Schlegel et al. (1998) value has been capped, the values are reported but no reddening is applied in calculating the T magnitude, and no derived stellar parameters are provided.
The CTL priority is reduced by a factor of 0.1 for stars within 10 degrees of the Galactic plane due to larger errors.
The fit residuals of the photometric color–Teff relation show a near-zero mean offset with an r.m.s. scatter of 122 K.
Given typical spectroscopic Teff uncertainties of ~100 K, the true scatter in the photometric relation is implied to be ~70 K.
The validity range of the color–Teff relation is GBP-GRP = [-0.2, +3.5].
Predictions from the color–Teff relation are likely less reliable for hot stars with GBP-GRP < 0 due to the steep slope, and for M stars with GBP-GRP > 2.
The CTL relies mainly on a specially curated Cool Dwarf list for cool dwarf stars and draws Teff estimates for those stars from that list.
The color–Teff relation provides a continuous relation from 3000 K to 15000 K; outside this range the TIC reports Teff = Null unless a spectroscopic Teff or a CTL-associated Teff is available.
Final Teff errors reported in the TIC include the 122 K scatter added in quadrature to uncertainties from photometric errors.
Stellar radii are computed using Gaia parallaxes via the standard Stefan-Boltzmann relation involving distance, extinction-corrected G magnitude, Teff, and bolometric correction in the Gaia passband.

Distance D is based on Gaia parallax from Bailer-Jones et al. (2018), G is extinction-corrected observed Gaia magnitude, Teff is from spectroscopy or dereddened colors, and BCG is the bolometric correction as a function of Teff.
For Teff from spectroscopy, 100 K is added in quadrature to the Teff uncertainty if the catalog-reported uncertainty is less than 100 K when computing mass and radius uncertainties.

For the 3300–8000 K range, polynomial formulae for BCG reported by the Gaia team (Andrae et al. 2018) based on MARCS models within 0.5 dex of solar metallicity are adopted, split into 3300–4000 K and 4000–8000 K segments with a +0.0036 mag shift applied to the cooler segment for continuity.

Above 8000 K up to 12000 K, a cubic polynomial is fit to bolometric corrections from PHOENIX stellar atmosphere models restricted to metallicities within 0.5 dex of solar and log g above 3.0, shifted by +0.01036 mag to match the Gaia polynomial at 8000 K, with a constant BCG error of 0.04 mag adopted.

The study provides polynomial relations to compute the Gaia G-band bolometric correction (BC_G) as a function of effective temperature for three ranges: below 4000 K, 4000–8000 K, and 8000–12000 K, along with corresponding uncertainty polynomials.

Stellar mass is inferred from effective temperature using revised spline relations for stars on or near the main sequence, applied only when the stellar radius places the star below the red giant branch and above the white dwarf sequence.
For stars cooler than 3300 K, stellar parameters are adopted from a specially curated Cool Dwarf list rather than extrapolating the Gaia polynomial relation.

To ensure internal consistency, dependent stellar properties such as log g, mean density, and bolometric luminosity are always calculated from the determined effective temperature, radius, and mass rather than using empirical measures from other catalogs.

The CTL assembly approach starts with approximately 1.7 billion stars in the TIC and applies cuts to select stars within desired apparent magnitude and spectral type ranges while eliminating evolved stars.

Stars are initially selected for the CTL if they have parallaxes and Gaia DR2 G, G_BP, and G_RP photometry satisfying quality criteria on reduced chi-squared, degrees of freedom, photometric excess factor, and color indices.
A TESS magnitude cut of T < 13 is applied to reduce the CTL to a manageable size, emphasizing bright dwarfs likely to be highest priority targets.
A specially curated Cool Dwarf List is used to ensure inclusion of high-priority M-dwarfs that would otherwise be eliminated by the T < 13 magnitude cut.

Stellar radius cuts are applied to eliminate red giants, explicitly including subgiants with 3.5 < log g < 4.1 but relying on prioritization metrics to prevent them from overwhelming final target selection.
For Teff >= 6000 K, the dividing line for radius cuts is log(R/R_sun) = 0.7, with subsequent piecewise linear nodes at (5000 K, 0.2) and (2000 K, 0.0).
Stars likely to be white dwarfs are excluded using a diagram of absolute G magnitude versus G_BP - G_RP color.
A color-magnitude boundary was defined by eye in the M_G vs G_BP - G_RP diagram to separate main sequence and white dwarf sequences, represented by the equation M_G = 5.15(G_BP - G_RP) + 4.12.
Stars falling below the defined color-magnitude boundary after proper reddening corrections are eliminated as probable white dwarfs.

Stars are excluded from the CTL if their effective temperature cannot be determined spectroscopically or from dereddened colors, or if their radius or flux contamination from nearby stars cannot be estimated, as these are essential for setting target priorities.
All stars in the specially curated Cool Dwarf and Hot Subdwarf target lists are included in the CTL.

Stars previously included in the TICv7 CTL based on reduced proper-motion cuts suggesting they are dwarfs are retained in the new CTL if Gaia DR2 does not provide sufficiently reliable information to warrant their exclusion.

Flux contamination is calculated by searching for contaminants within 10 TESS pixels of the target and computing contaminating flux within a magnitude-dependent radius using a pre-launch PSF model from SPOC; the reported value is the ratio of total contaminant flux to target star flux.

A Monte Carlo approach is implemented to improve final uncertainty estimates for stellar parameters by perturbing each observed quantity 1000 times and carrying perturbed values through calculations to obtain distributions for each derived quantity.
The 16th and 84th percentiles of the Monte Carlo derived distributions are reported as the corresponding lower and upper error bars to reflect asymmetric parameter posteriors.

Once a quantity is perturbed in the Monte Carlo procedure, the same perturbed value is used throughout to preserve parameter correlations; asymmetric errors are handled by assuming Gaussian distributions on each side.

The Monte Carlo procedure sequentially perturbs the stellar distance using normal Gaussian deviates and then perturbs the reddening based on contributions from both distance and intrinsic dust map errors.

The method perturbs the (B-V) color by adding Gaussian noise scaled by the low and high reddening uncertainties, then calculates reddening and extinction in Gaia passbands using E(G_BP-G_RP)' = 1.31 E(B-V)' and A(G)' = 2.72 E(B-V)'.
Gaia color and magnitude are perturbed using photometric errors: (G_BP-G_RP)' = (G_BP-G_RP) + N×σ_G_BP + N×σ_G_RP, and G' = G + N×σ_G.
The perturbed Gaia color and magnitude are dereddened by subtracting the calculated reddening and extinction values.

The perturbed and dereddened TESS magnitude is computed using dereddened Gaia magnitude and color, with perturbed T-band extinction applied as A(T)' = 2.06 E(B-V)'. The final apparent TESS magnitude includes this extinction plus scatter from the T calibration.
The perturbed effective temperature is computed by adding Gaussian noise to the perturbed dereddened temperature, where σ_Teff = 122 K.
The perturbed stellar radius is computed from the perturbed bolometric correction, effective temperature, distance, and dereddened Gaia magnitude.

The catalog includes calculated TESS magnitudes.
Adopted effective temperatures (in K) are provided along with their sources and errors estimated via Monte Carlo methods.
Stellar radii and masses derived from photometry are included in solar units, with uncertainties and asymmetric Monte Carlo errors.
A contamination ratio representing the flux from neighboring stars relative to the target star is provided.
The catalog flags whether a star has been observed in 2-minute cadence and lists the sector or combination of sectors where it was observed.
Galactic and Ecliptic longitudes and latitudes in degrees are recorded for each star.
Parallaxes from TGAS/Gaia or Hipparcos, distances in parsecs, and total proper motions in mas/yr are provided with associated uncertainties including Monte Carlo estimates.
Photometric magnitudes from multiple surveys are included: V band, 2MASS JHKs, Gaia G/BP/RP, SDSS ugriz, and ALLWISE W1-W4.
Cross-identifiers include Hipparcos Number, Tycho-2 ID, 2MASS ID, and TICID from the TESS Input Catalog.
A flag identifies whether a star belongs to a special list.

Priority values are computed based on TIC-4, TIC-5, and TIC-6 schemas, as well as variants without neighbor contamination and without sector boosting, incorporating radius and flux contamination boosts and de-boosts.
Applied extinction E(B-V) values are provided with errors and source identification.
Additional stellar parameters include surface gravity (log g), density, luminosity, and metallicity, each with uncertainties and source identifiers.
Noise terms include uncertainties from star counts, sky counts, neighboring star counts, detector readout, and a systematics floor.

evidence.quote_or_value: Abstract We describe the catalogs assembled and the algorithms used to populate the revised TESS Input Catalog (TIC), based on the incorporation of the Gaia second data release. We also describe a revised ranking system for prioritizing stars for 2 minute cadence observations, and we assemble a revised Candidate Target List (CTL) using that ranking. The TIC is available on the Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes server, and an enhanced CTL is available through the Filtergraph data visualization portal system at http://filtergraph.vanderbilt.edu/tess_ctl .
